questions.text: Why does this lesson keep fixturePassed separate from productionReady?

options.A: A fixture pass proves all hosts will discover and execute the skill correctly.
options.B: Production readiness depends only on whether the package has a version number.
options.C: Locally recomputed hashes authenticate the evaluator’s capture claims automatically.
options.D: Fixture success proves gate mechanics, while production claims need captured evidence and an external trust anchor.

questions.explanation: Deterministic fixtures test the gate. Local integrity can be recomputed by the package editor, so production readiness additionally requires externally trusted evidence attestation.

questions.text: You compare task quality with and without a skill. Which experiment best attributes a difference to the skill?

options.A: Use a stronger model only for the skill condition.
options.B: Hold model, tools, fixtures, sampling policy, and budgets constant across repeated paired runs.
options.C: Give the skill condition extra tool access and compare only token counts.
options.D: Compare one curated skill demo against unrelated historical tasks.

questions.explanation: Paired runs with controlled conditions isolate the skill’s contribution. Repetition exposes variability and per-task regressions.

questions.text: classification_metrics receives expected=[True, True, False, False] and predicted=[True, False, True, False]. What precision and recall does it return?
questions.explanation: There is one true positive, one false positive, and one false negative. Precision=1/(1+1)=0.5 and recall=1/(1+1)=0.5.
